notes: Copy this file, remove _instructions, and fill in your real data.
All fields marked REQUIRED must be present. Optional fields can be omitted.
abbreviation: short code used in formula notation (e.g. 'W' for white, 'UB' for ultramarine blue). Same color concept should use the same abbreviation across all brands.
hex_color: CSS hex color for the paint swatch, e.g. '#A3B2C1'. Leave empty string if unknown.
parts: numeric quantity — use integers where possible (3 not 3.0). Decimals allowed (1.5).
parts can also be 'Δ' (or 'delta' / 'trace') for a quantity too small to measure — a trace amount. Use this instead of a number when the recipe calls for the mathematical delta symbol.
date_start / date_end: year CE as integer, e.g. 800. Use null if unknown.
page_reference: folio, chapter, or page, e.g. 'folio 12r' or 'chapter III'. Empty string if none.
The command is idempotent — safe to re-run after database resets (uses get_or_create throughout).

pigments.name: Red Ochre
pigments.description: Mineral powder composed from Iron Oxide (mostly Hematite) created by heating up Yellow Ochre

pigments.name: Azurite
pigments.description: Mineral pigment formed by Copper Carbonate, is usually found alongside its green variant Malachite. While lightfast and stable at moment of painting, after long times the blue can turn green because the Copper Carbonate in Malachite is chemically more stable than Azurite. This process can also happen in acidic or sulfur rich environments.

pigments.name: Bohemian Green
pigments.description: Named after the region of Bohemia where it was tradicionally extracted, this green comes from a mix of minerals rich in Glauconite creates a semi transparent olive green color.

pigments.name: Yellow Ochre
pigments.description: Mineral powder composed from Iron Oxide (mostly Goethite) with small parts of silica and clay. it can be heated to ~400C to transform the Goethite into Hematite, converting the yellow in Red Ochre
